Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Gray","(B) Green","(C) Black","(D) White","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/03751_Toronto.png"}},"question":"What color is the building with two maple leaf patterns on the top right area of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building",pattern="two maple leaf patterns"))
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)

n2=LOCATE($n1,T("ship"))
n3=SELECT_ORD($n2,null,2,TOP_TO_BOTTOM)
n4=ATTRIBUTE($n3,"color")
FINAL($n4,CHOICE_SINGLE)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Blue","(B) Red","(C) White","(D) Black","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P10090.png"}},"question":"What color is the car on the vertical road at the left edge of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("car"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the car on the vertical road at the left edge of the picture",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),

and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,

MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Blue","(B) White","(C) Purple","(D) Black","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11193.png"}},"question":"What color is the brown building roof on the right side of the new circular road in the lower right corner of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("building",color="brown"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the brown building roof on the right side of the new circular road in the lower right corner of the picture",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color","roof")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,

source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION

multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Red","(B) Yellow","(C) Silver-gray","(D) Green","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P6846.png"}},"question":"What color is the car located inside the traffic wheel in the bottom left corner of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("car"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the car located inside the traffic wheel in the bottom left corner of the picture",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

INTENT(SIMPLE_COUNT)
n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=COUNT($n1,T("car",color="red"),false)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,

and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n4=GROUP($n3,CLUSTER)
n5=SELECT_SEM($n4,null,"the group of three closely situated lakes",SINGLE,$image0)
n6=RELATION($n2,$n5)
FINAL($n6,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

INTENT(OBJECT_RELATION)
n1=REGION($image0,BOTTOM_LEFT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building",color="white",shape="rectangular"))
n3=LOCATE($n1,T("building",color="gray",shape="rectangular"))
n4=SELECT_SEM($n3,null,"the longest gray rectangular building in the cluster of houses in the lower left corner of the picture",SINGLE,$n1)
n5=RELATION($n2,$n4)
FINAL($n5,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,

and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and

alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Factory or Power Plant","(B) Port","(C) Airport Terminal","(D) Multi-unit residential buildings"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"DOTA_v2_4096_4096/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11151.png"}},"question":"Select the options that best represent the types of land use depicted in the image.","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(MULTILABEL_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY($image0,["Factory or Power Plant","Port","Airport Terminal","Multi-unit residential buildings"])
FINAL($n1,CHOICE_MULTI)

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

n1=REGION_BBOX($image0,[5322.0,6073.0,5573.0,6356.0])

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,

MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Red","(B) White","(C) Green","(D) Black","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P7078.png"}},"question":"What color is the right rectangular open space next to the dock in the lower left area of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("open space",shape="rectangular"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the right rectangular open space next to the dock in the lower left area of the picture",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,

MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("ring",shape="circular"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the circular ring at the center of the green hexagon on the docked ship in the bottom left corner of the picture",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex

evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n7=SELECT_REL($n6,$n5,INSIDE)

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

INTENT(RELATIONAL_COUNT)
n1=REGION($image0,BOTTOM_LEFT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("board",color="red"))

n4=SELECT_REL($n3,$n2,NEXT_TO)
n5=COUNT_ENTITIES($n4,T("ship"),false)
FINAL($n5,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n1=REGION($image0,BOTTOM)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("waterway"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,null,"the widest waterway at the bottom of the picture",SINGLE,$n1)
n4=LOCATE($image0,T("ship"))
n5=SELECT_REL($n4,$n3,INSIDE)
n6=COUNT_ENTITIES($n5,T("ship"),false)
FINAL($n6,CHOICE_SINGLE)

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) 9","(B) 7","(C) 6","(D) 4","(E) This image doesn't feature the count."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P6281.png"}},"question":"How many cars are parking on the top of the building in the bottom right corner of this picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(RELATIONAL_COUNT)
n1=REGION($image0,BOTTOM_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building"))
n3=LOCATE($n1,T("car"))
n4=SELECT_REL($n3,$n2,ABOVE)
n5=COUNT_ENTITIES($n4,T("car"),false)
FINAL($n5,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n3=SELECT_REL($n2,$n1,RIGHT_OF)
n4=SELECT_RANK($n3,null,"area",1,DESCENDING)

FINAL($n7,CHOICE_SINGLE)

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) 5","(B) 4","(C) 6","(D) 8","(E) This image doesn't feature the count."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P9702.png"}},"question":"How many cars are there in the rooftop parking lot at the bottom left of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(RELATIONAL_COUNT)
n1=REGION($image0,BOTTOM_LEFT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("rooftop parking lot"))
n3=LOCATE($image0,T("car"))
n4=SELECT_REL($n3,$n2,INSIDE)
n5=COUNT_ENTITIES($n4,T("car"),false)
FINAL($n5,CHOICE_SINGLE)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,

MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("building"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the highest building in the picture",SINGLE,$image0)

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,

ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n5=RELATION($n3,$n4)

The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building",color="gray",shape="rectangular"))

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Below","(B) Above","(C) Lower left corner","(D) Top left corner"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD/2006/35-2006-0360-6775-LA93.tif"}},"question":"What is the orientation of the building with the largest white rectangular roof, featuring numerous vents, located next to the highway in relation to the red and green tennis courts in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OBJECT_RELATION)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("highway"))
n2=LOCATE($image0,T("building",has_part="white rectangular roof, numerous vents"))
n3=SELECT_REL($n2,$n1,NEXT_TO)
n4=SELECT_SEM($n3,null,"the building next to the highway with the largest white rectangular roof featuring numerous vents",SINGLE,$image0)
n5=LOCATE($image0,T("tennis court",color="red and green"))
n6=RELATION($n4,$n5)
FINAL($n6,CHOICE_SINGLE)

contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Black","(B) Blue","(C) Yellow","(D) Orange"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"ITCVD/00147.jpg"}},"question":"Determine the color of the object within the given reference bounding box in the satellite image. Image resolution: 5616 x 3744. Bounding box: [1726, 1062, 1787, 1098].","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=REGION_BBOX($image0,[1726.0,1062.0,1787.0,1098.0],[5616,3744])
n2=ATTRIBUTE($n1,"color")
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)

single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

INTENT(CHANGE_COUNT)
n1=FIND_MARKER($image0,"circle","red")
n2=LOCATE($image0,T("farm"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,$n1,"the farm candidates within the areas marked by the referenced red circles in this image",MULTI,$image0)
n4=COUNT_ENTITIES($n3,T("farm"),false)
n5=FIND_MARKER($image1,"circle","red")
n6=LOCATE($image1,T("farm"))
n7=SELECT_SEM($n6,$n5,"the farm candidates within the areas marked by the referenced red circles in this image",MULTI,$image1)
n8=COUNT_ENTITIES($n7,T("farm"),false)
n9=ABS_DIFF($n4,$n8)
FINAL($n9,CHOICE_SINGLE)
