messages.content:
Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) 2","(B) 1","(C) 4","(D) 3"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD-5/35-2006-0375-6815-LA93-changing1.tif"},"image1":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD-5/35-2012-0375-6815-LA93-0M50-E080-changing2.tif"}},"question":"In the areas marked by red circles in the two images, how many differences are there between the buildings?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(CHANGE_COUNT)
n1=FIND_MARKER($image0,"circle","red")
n2=LOCATE($image0,T("building"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,$n1,"the building candidates within the areas marked by the referenced red circles in this image",MULTI,$image0)
n4=COUNT_ENTITIES($n3,T("building"),false)
n5=FIND_MARKER($image1,"circle","red")
n6=LOCATE($image1,T("building"))
n7=SELECT_SEM($n6,$n5,"the building candidates within the areas marked by the referenced red circles in this image",MULTI,$image1)
n8=COUNT_ENTITIES($n7,T("building"),false)
n9=ABS_DIFF($n4,$n8)
FINAL($n9,CHOICE_SINGLE)

(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only

SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).

attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) On the left side","(B) Above","(C) Upper right corner","(D) Top left corner"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD/2012/35-2012-0335-6810-LA93-0M50-E080.tif"}},"question":"In the cluster of buildings near the bottom edge on the right side of the image, what is the position of the longest gray rectangular building relative to the largest deep blue irregular building?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OBJECT_RELATION)
n1=REGION($image0,BOTTOM_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building",color="gray",shape="rectangular"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,null,"the longest gray rectangular building in the cluster of buildings near the bottom edge on the right side of the image",SINGLE,$n1)
n4=LOCATE($n1,T("building",color="deep blue",shape="irregular"))
n5=SELECT_RANK($n4,null,"bbox_area",1,DESCENDING)
n6=RELATION($n3,$n5)
FINAL($n6,CHOICE_SINGLE)

optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

n2=LOCATE($n1,T("park",color="green"))

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) In the middle position on the right side of the picture","(B) In the upper left area of the picture","(C) In the upper right area of the picture","(D) In the lower left area of the picture","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P4177.png"}},"question":"Where are the two adjacent black disc-shaped buildings located in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("building",color="black",shape="disc-shaped"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the two adjacent black disc-shaped buildings",MULTI,$image0)
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"Where in the original image is the selected target or target group?")

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) White","(B) Yellow","(C) Red","(D) Blue","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P10499.png"}},"question":"What color is the car that is not parked in the parking lot area between two buildings in the center of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("car"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the car that is not parked in the parking lot area between two buildings in the center",SINGLE,$image0)
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"What color or colors are visible on the selected object or objects?")

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) In the upper right area of the picture","(B) In the lower right area of the picture","(C) In the middle of the right side of the picture","(D) In bottom center of the picture","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P4189.png"}},"question":"Where is the rainbow zebra crossing in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("zebra crossing"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the rainbow zebra crossing",SINGLE,$image0)
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"Where in the original image is the selected target or target group?")

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) In the middle of the right area of the picture","(B) In the upper left area of the picture","(C) In the middle of the left of the picture","(D) In the upper left area of the picture","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P9191.png"}},"question":"Where is the playground with a circular pattern on the ground in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("playground",pattern="circular ground pattern"))
FINAL_QUESTION($n1,CHOICE_SINGLE,"Where is the playground with a circular pattern on the ground in the picture?")

messages.content:
Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) At the top on the right side of this picture","(B) At the bottom on the left side of this picture","(C) In the middle on the right side of this picture","(D) In the middle on the left side of this picture","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P9653.png"}},"question":"Where is the building with grey roof located in this picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("building"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the building with grey roof",SINGLE,$image0)
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"Where in the original image is the selected target or target group?")

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Red and blue","(B) Green and white","(C) Blue and white","(D) Yellow and green","(E) The image does not feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P2827.png"}},"question":"What main color is the large freighter in the water on the left of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=REGION($image0,LEFT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("freighter",size="large"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,null,"the large freighter in the water on the left of the picture",SINGLE,$n1)
n4=ATTRIBUTE($n3,"color")
FINAL($n4,CHOICE_SINGLE)

{"choices":["(A) Green","(B) Black","(C) White","(D) Red","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P4101.png"}},"question":"What is the color of the boat at the bottom of the water area in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) White","(B) Pink","(C) Green","(D) Orange","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P3861.png"}},"question":"What color is the roof of the row of buildings in the upper right corner of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("building"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,null,"the row of buildings in the upper right corner",MULTI,$n1)
FINAL_QUESTION($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE,"What color or colors are visible on the roof of the selected target or targets?")

and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) To the left","(B) Top left corner","(C) To the right","(D) Above"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"DOTA_v2_4096_4096/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P3013.png"}},"question":"In the image, what is the position of the largest orange building within the green rectangular area?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("building",color="orange"))
n2=SELECT_RANK($n1,null,"bbox_area",1,DESCENDING)
n3=LOCATE($image0,T("area",color="green",shape="rectangular"))
n4=RELATION($n2,$n3)
FINAL($n4,CHOICE_SINGLE)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Global warming has intensified the melting of polar glaciers, leading to a rise in sea levels.","(B) Sometimes, changes in river water levels can cause previously submerged land to emerge above the surface, forming small islands.","(C) The flow of river water erodes the riverbanks and also carries materials such as silt, depositing them in areas with slower currents to form islands.","(D) Human activities sometimes intentionally or unintentionally create artificial islands in rivers."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"MiniFrance/44-2013-0375-6705-LA93-0M50-E080.jp2.tif"}},"question":"Why are there many small islands on both sides of the river in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=VLM_REASON(image=$image0,question="Why are there many small islands on both sides of the river in the picture?",choices="$choices")
FINAL($n1,CHOICE_MULTI)

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Upper right side","(B) Right Side","(C) On the left side","(D) Upper Side"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD/2012/35-2012-0365-6775-LA93-0M50-E080.tif"}},"question":"In the image, the triangular parking lot located towards the lower right side is positioned at which direction relative to the circular roundabout?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("parking lot",shape="triangular"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the triangular parking lot located towards the lower right side",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=LOCATE($image0,T("roundabout",shape="circular"))
n4=RELATION($n2,$n3)
FINAL($n4,CHOICE_SINGLE)
